name: ecoli_dec
description: Diarrheagenic E. coli marker panel (GB 4789.6 + risk-monitoring designation)

references.citation: Kaper JB, Nataro JP, Mobley HL. Pathogenic Escherichia coli. Nat Rev Microbiol 2004;2(2):123-40.
references.note: The pathotype framework (EHEC, STEC, EPEC, ETEC, EIEC, EAEC) the scheme's ladder implements.

references.citation: GB 4789.6-2016, National food safety standard: microbiological examination of food — examination of diarrheagenic Escherichia coli (China).
references.note: The five-marker designation the gb4789_6 scheme follows, including its uidA genus control.

caveats: Pathotypes are not mutually exclusive: escV plus stx is EHEC, stx without escV is STEC, and a strain carrying both EAEC and STEC markers is a hybrid that reports only the higher-severity call (the other one lands in RUNNER_UP).
uidA is the genus control, not a pathotype marker. uidA-negative isolates (some EIEC/Shigella) fail the control gate and report the fallback with 'control gene absent' rather than 'non-DEC'.

pic and astA have close homologs outside EAEC, which is why the database ships a 90% identity floor for pic in floors.json; a single pic hit above the default 80% threshold is not by itself an EAEC call.

stx subtyping stops at stx1a/stx1b/stx2a/stx2b. stx2c, stx2d and other variants fold into presence of the nearest recorded subfamily, so subtype-level epidemiology (e.g. stx2a vs stx2d severity) needs a dedicated subtyping tool.
A pathotype call is a marker profile, not a phenotype: no marker panel proves toxin expression, and isolates can lose or acquire these genes on mobile elements.
